title: fix(core): refuse a non-Date exotic comparand instead of dropping the field (objectui#8567)
body:
Fixes #8567

`convertFiltersToAST`'s operator-object arm opens on `typeof value === 'object'` and then iterates `Object.entries(value)`. `Object.entries` of a `RegExp`, a `Set`, a `Map` or a `URL` is `[]`, so the loop body never ran and **no condition was pushed for that field**: `{ status: 'a', created: /abc/ }` lowered to `['status', '=', 'a']`. Nothing threw, nothing warned, and the result set got **wider** than the author asked for. objectui#8555 closed the `Date` door of that hole; this closes the rest of it.

## What changed

The arm now classifies every object value totally, in three cases instead of two:

| value | answer | why |
|---|---|---|
| an accepted comparand (`Date`) | lowered to `[field, '=', value]` | the spec rules it IN (objectui#8555) |
| a **plain** object (`{}`, `{ $gte: 1 }`, a null-prototype bag, a cross-realm plain object) | read as an operator map, exactly as before | `{}` is the TRUE identity and constrains nothing (objectui#5322) |
| anything else — `RegExp`, `Set`, `Map`, `URL`, a class instance | **refused**, `FilterOperatorError` / `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 | the spec rules it OUT |

The gate is the value's **prototype**, not `Object.keys(value).length === 0`. Zero own entries is exactly what `{}` and `/x/` have in common, and they need opposite answers — a key count cannot tell them apart, and a fix built on one sweeps up the identity. The second prototype hop admits cross-realm plain objects, whose prototype is another realm's `Object.prototype`.

Measured against `@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0 (declared floor `^17.2.0`, and `ACCEPTED_FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPES_SENTENCE` verified present in the 17.2.0 tarball, not assumed): `isAcceptedFilterComparand(/x/)` is `false`, and `normalizeFilterComparandTypes({ created: /x/ })` answers `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 — *"Filter comparand at where.created is a RegExp instance ({}), which no driver can compare."* So lowering would only move the refusal downstream; the answer the wire would give two layers later is given here, where the field name and the offending value are still in hand.

## The refusal CLASS — the assumption in the brief, tested

The dispatch assumed this file's existing `FilterOperatorError` refusals are the same class as this one and that the idiom could be copied. **Read rather than counted, that is half right.** The file has seven throw sites, and they are not one class:

- `$regex` and the unknown-operator arm — **operator vocabulary**: the spelling is absent from the spec's `FILTER_OPERATORS`, so there is nothing to translate it into;
- `$not` — **AST expressiveness**: the spec *declares* it, but the array dialect this file emits has no negation keyword;
- the two `lowerLogicalGroup` throws — **combinator argument shape**, against the spec's declared `'$and?: FilterCondition[]'`;
- the bare-array arm and the stored-rule arity arm — **comparand shape**, argued from downstream behaviour *precisely because the spec declines to rule* (`assertListComparandShapes` rules only on `$in` / `$nin` / `$between`).

This one is none of those: it is a comparand **type** the spec itself rejects — the opposite authority to its nearest neighbour. So the `$regex` / `$not` message idiom ("this layer has no target for your operator") is deliberately **not** copied: a reader who wrote `{ name: /abc/ }` used no operator at all, and that sentence would answer a question they did not ask. What *is* shared is the error **type**, and on a measurement rather than on its name — four of the seven existing throws are already non-operator refusals, because what `FilterOperatorError` transports is the `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 envelope `classifyLoadError` reads. A bare `Error` there classifies as a network fault. Both halves are pinned in section 4 of the new test.

## Verification

Everything below is a real run in a dedicated worktree at `42ddd7f71`.

- **Full `unit` project** (`pnpm exec vitest run --project unit`): `1029 passed | 2 skipped`, `17647 passed | 4 skipped`.
- **DOM-side filter consumers** (app-shell, plugin-detail ×2, plugin-grid ×2, plugin-view, plugin-map, fields ×2): `9 passed`, `80 passed`.
- **Type-check** (`turbo run type-check`, core + data-objectstack): `5 successful, 5 total`. core's `type-check` is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test file is type-checked too.
- **Full workspace lint** (`turbo run lint`): `47 successful, 47 total`, 0 errors. `filter-converter.ts` carries 7 `no-explicit-any` warnings both before and after (measured against the `HEAD` file through `--stdin`), so this diff adds none. No narrowing to declare — the complete run went green.
- **Gates**, each read from the gate's own verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe: `check:control-bytes` 0 · `check:spec-symbols` 0 · `check:doc-fences` 0 · `check:doc-types` 0 · `check:doc-examples` 0 (125 blocks, 90 ledger rows, none moved) · `check:doc-snippets` 0 (638/638) · `check:readme-exports` 0 · `check:unreferenced-sources` 0 · `check-doc-links` 0 · `check-changeset-presence` / `-no-major` / `-overwrite` 0.
  - ⚠️ `check:readme-exports`, `check:doc-examples` and `check:doc-snippets` first exited non-zero on an **unbuilt** tree (`packagesRead: found 6, floor is 25`). That is a prerequisite, not a finding: the whole workspace was built (`turbo run build`, 43/43) and all three then ran green. The first result is recorded as NOT MEASURED, not as a failure.
- A manual control-character sweep (`grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'`) over all five changed files found none.

### Ablation and control — run against the committed tree

Each leg was proved on disk **before** it was run (`git hash-object` off the `HEAD` blob, plus the anchored marker count) and restored **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty and the blob back at `5ba58fb`). No rebuild step: `vitest.config.mts` aliases `@object-ui/core` to `packages/core/src`, so these tests execute the source and there is no `dist/` hop a stale build could make silently green.

| leg | on-disk proof | result | mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| refusal branch removed (16 lines) | blob `5ba58fb` → `7458ef8`; marker `!isOperatorMap(value)` 1 → 0 | **10 of 34 red**, across both files | the refusal is MISSING and fails as the defect itself — `convertFiltersToAST({ created: /abc/ })` hands back `{ created: /abc/ }`, the original object, because `conditions` ended empty |
| gate swapped for `Object.keys(value).length === 0` | blob `5ba58fb` → `d3a3e70`; injected text 1, removed text 0 | **4 of 34 red** | over-refusal — `{}` is swept up, so **both** `{}` identity controls redden |

**The control behaves as a control.** The `{}` TRUE identity — this repo's, pinned in `filter-date-comparand-8555.test.ts` since objectui#8555 — stayed **green** through the ablation leg and went **red** under the caricature. It moves when the change is wrong and does not move when the subject is merely absent, which is the difference between a control and a second copy of the subject.

## Enumeration — two axes

**Content — who reads what this change says.** The `RegExp` negative in `filter-date-comparand-8555.test.ts` (it pinned the silent drop as a `.not.toEqual(...)`; it now pins the envelope, and it was going to break either way) · `packages/data-objectstack/src/readme-filter-operator-table.test.ts`, which reads `filter-converter.ts` **source** (anchored on `const operatorMap`, unmoved and unreshaped here) and executes every README refused-table row · the other five filter tests in `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/` · the three `ValueDataSource.*FilterVocabulary` / `filterLogicConformance` tests that assert parity with this lowering · the runtime callers of `convertFiltersToAST` / `toFilterNode` / `mergeFilterNodes` in app-shell, components, core, fields, react, plugin-detail, plugin-form, plugin-grid, plugin-list, plugin-map, plugin-timeline and plugin-view — all covered by the two test runs above.

**Position — who points at these files by `file:line`, and what lines moved.** Two rows exist and both were checked rather than assumed:

- `docs/audits/2901-spec-enum-renderer-coverage.md:150` names `filter-converter.ts:126` in its link *text*. **Line 126 does not move**: the import was kept on one line for exactly this reason, and the first line-shifting hunk is at 198. (Separately, that reference was already stale before this PR — line 126 is inside `lowerLogicalGroup`, not the `Unknown filter operator` throw the sentence describes. Noted below, not filed and not fixed here.)
- `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs:289` names `packages/data-objectstack/README.md:603-606`, and this PR inserts 17 lines at README line 192, so those lines shift to 620-623. It is prose, not an enforced ledger, and it is explicitly **dated** to commit `c30026715` with the instrument for re-deriving it named beside it — a dated reading about that commit stays true about that commit. The same docblock's own reproduction records that package READMEs are not in this gate's scan population. `check:doc-types` was run anyway: exit 0.

Nothing else in the tree names these paths with a line number. `check:doc-examples`'s ledger is keyed `path:line symbol`, and it has **no row** for `filter-converter.ts` (it has no fenced `@example`; the file's examples are bare, which that gate counts and never compiles) — and this diff moves lines in no file that carries a row.

## Clause-② — measured, not inherited: **no**

The mechanical floor is not tripped: **no new exported symbol** (`isOperatorMap` and `describeExoticComparand` are module-private; `FilterOperatorError` was already exported) and **no new key on a published payload**. On the directional criterion the accept set is **narrowed**, not widened, and it is narrowed to a contract the spec has already published — the paradigm "pulling code back to the declared contract" case, quoted here as `ACCEPTED_FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPES` = `['string','number','bigint','boolean','null','Date']` with `isAcceptedFilterComparand(/x/) === false`.

`node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration no --diff <this diff>` → **exit 0**, *"5 changed file(s) read, no widening tell on any declared surface."* ⚠️ Read honestly, that CLI has no `--repo` flag and defaults to `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, so an objectui diff is judged against objectstack's surfaces. Re-run through the module API with `repo: 'objectstack-ai/objectui'`, the three changed source/doc paths are on **no** declared surface either, while the control path `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts` **is** covered by the objectui mirror row — so the green is a reading, not an artefact of repo scoping.

⚠️ The card's fixed-spelling `Clause-②:` line is **absent from the claim comment**, and the PM seat has no tool to edit an existing comment. That is a protocol gap, reported rather than papered over: a second claim comment would turn `missing` into `misplaced`, which fails identically while looking answered. No `needs:contract-review` label is attached, because the measured declaration is `no`.

## 验收备注

Facts measured while working on this card, deliberately **not** ridden into this PR:

- `docs/audits/2901-spec-enum-renderer-coverage.md:150` points at `filter-converter.ts:126` for a `$ncontains` claim, and line 126 has not held that code for some time. *noted, not filed* — successor: the same audit's item 4 (`FilterConditionField.tsx` emitting `{ $ncontains: value }`, a token the spec does not carry) touches that paragraph when it is fixed.
- `packages/data-objectstack/README.md`'s "Refused at lowering time" **table** gains no row for this refusal, deliberately: `readme-filter-operator-table.test.ts` executes each row's example through `JSON.parse` (`No eval`, by design), and no exotic comparand can be written as a JSON literal — a row would redden the pin with "cannot parse the example literal". The refusal is documented in prose immediately under the table instead, where the pin does not read it. *noted, not filed*; successor: whoever wants the refused table to be exhaustive over non-`$` shapes needs a second example channel first.

## 维护者速读（草稿）

**改了什么** — `convertFiltersToAST` 遇到 `RegExp` / `Set` / `Map` / `URL` / 类实例这类"外来对象"当比较值时,不再静默丢掉这个字段,而是抛 `FilterOperatorError`(`INVALID_FILTER` / 400),消息点名字段和值,并给出能用的写法。

**为什么改** — 丢掉一个条件 = 查询结果比作者要求的更宽,而且什么都不报。这是列表/相关列表悄悄多出记录的那一类故障。spec 自己已经判了这类值不可比较,所以这里只是把两层之后才会给出的同一个答复提前给,给在字段名和值都还在手上的地方。

**风险与代价(含回滚)** — 以前不抛的调用现在会抛,这是已发布行为的改变;但抛出的信封与本文件既有的三处拒绝完全一致,`classifyLoadError` 认得它,失败会渲染成"过滤器有问题"而不是"检查网络"。只有手写代码才会产生这类值(来自元数据的过滤器经 JSON 解析,永远是普通对象),仓内实测没有任何生产路径这样写。回滚 = revert 本 PR,无数据迁移、无 schema 变更。

**席位意见** — （留空,待复核席位填写）

**你要做的** — 无需操作。若你在 app 代码里写过 `{ 字段: /正则/ }` 这样的过滤器,它以前就不生效(条件被丢弃),现在会明确报错;按错误消息改成 `$contains` / `$startsWith` / `$in` 即可。
